source.title: In-Context Learning can distort the relationship between sequence likelihoods and biological fitness
source.authors: Pranav Kantroo; Gunter P. Wagner; B. Machta

page_placements.theme: Induction-like copying in other modalities and non-autoregressive models

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests induction-like retrieval in biological sequence models and contexts, extending the question to masked protein and RNA models and to other architectures.
record.gate_note: The paper measures sequence-level retrieval and uncertainty changes, not attention-head formation, head circuits, training-time emergence, an in-context-learning loss-by-token-index effect, or few-shot task learning. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures model-level copying from repeated context (pseudo-perplexity collapse, look-up of the equivalent residue) in protein and RNA language models at inference. It never identifies attention heads, previous-token composition or circuits, and the authors say the circuits in bidirectional models 'may differ'. Several models (CARP, LC-PLM) have no attention heads at all. No training trajectory is followed and training data is not manipulated, so neither V4 (heads across families) nor V5 (data or training dependence of head formation) is tested. The induction-head link is an analogy the authors draw. The findings belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that in-context retrieval on repeated motifs distorts the likelihood–fitness relationship and can override learned priors. It extends to imperfect repeats and hairpin-like motifs, and varies across architectures, with transformers most affected. They call it only 'spiritually similar' to induction heads and do not analyse circuits.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates masked and autoregressive biological sequence models on repeated-sequence contexts and pseudo-perplexity or prediction uncertainty. It does not reproduce the original synthetic training-time induction-head experiments or analyze attention-head circuits.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with architecture, repeat-unit length and multiplicity, sequence context pattern, and RiNALMo model size; ESM2 retrieval also varies with target position in the ambiguous retrieval setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Transformer protein and RNA language models (ESM2 8M and 650M, Progen2-M, RiNALMo) show strong copying from repeated context: pseudo-perplexity collapses to about 1 for doubled sequences, and retrieval overrides learned priors. A convolutional model (CARP) collapses only for repeats under about 70 residues, and a BiMamba model (LC-PLM) shows only a progressive decline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-level induction-like copying of repeated context appears in biological sequence models, strongest in transformers, and varies by architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: RiNALMo retrieves from direct repeats and from reversed complements (hairpin-like motifs, complete collapse in 650M, partial in 33.5M), but not from reversed-only or complement-only context. The authors read this as dependence on training-data statistics, but without manipulating the training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which context transformations trigger in-context retrieval depends on patterns common in the training data and on model size.

record.problems: The study infers retrieval from sequence-level prediction and pseudo-perplexity outcomes rather than identifying attention heads or circuits. It does not manipulate training data or follow models during training. Many results are described qualitatively without exact numerical values or uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: No heads, previous-token composition or [A][B]…[A]→[B] circuit is analysed.
No attribution of in-context learning to heads, and no loss-by-token-index measure.
Heads with induction behaviour are never identified; only whole-model copying behaviour is shown.
Training data and setup are not varied, and head formation over training is not tracked.
Few-shot task learning is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 and V5 links were removed. The study shows behaviour of whole models, not heads; two of the models lack attention entirely; and the data dependence is inferred, not tested by changing training data.

versions.untested_parts: Does not identify or test attention heads, composition with a previous-token head, or the autoregressive [A][B] … [A] → [B] mechanism.
No training trajectory, abrupt head formation, in-context-learning loss-by-token-index gain, or training-loss bump is measured.
Does not measure how much in-context learning in large transformers is attributable to induction heads, or loss falling with token index.

Measures sequence-level retrieval-like behavior across selected models, but does not identify induction heads or test multiple training runs; model coverage is limited to the named biological sequence models.
Tests context-pattern and model differences, not changes to the training dataset or training procedure, nor when heads form or whether in-context learning persists over training.
Does not compare few-shot task learning with copying, or test whether other heads or mechanisms carry few-shot learning.
Does not track training transitions or test whether head formation consists of multiple sub-steps.

rows.subject: ESM2 (650M)
rows.stage_stated: trained on the masked language modeling objective
rows.operation_detail: Compared pseudo-perplexity for natural protein domains and their doubled sequences.

conditions.value: 2x sequence made by appending a copy

rows.value: The 2x sequences have pseudo-perplexity approximately one, described as a complete uncertainty collapse.
rows.note: The paper states the outcome in the text; no exact distribution values are given.
rows.check: Model-level pseudo-perplexity collapse in ESM2; no head-level measure, so it does not bear on V4 or V5.

conditions.value: 2x sequence made by appending a copy

rows.value: The model also exhibits an uncertainty collapse for doubled sequences.
rows.note: The paper says the behavior is not exclusive to larger-scale models.
rows.check: Same as r1; behaviour of the whole model, not heads.

source_check.locator_found: Results §2.1, paragraph introducing ESM2 (8M); Figure 2A; Methods.

rows.subject: Progen2-M (called Progen-M in Figure 2)
rows.operation_detail: Compared perplexity for natural protein domains and their doubled sequences.

conditions.value: 2x sequence made by appending a copy

rows.value: Perplexity drops significantly after sequences are doubled; the decline is not a complete collapse.
rows.note: The paper attributes the weaker effect relative to bidirectional masked models to autoregressive access only to preceding context.
rows.check: Autoregressive repeat-perplexity drop is induction-like behaviour, but no head is identified; not V4 as stated.

rows.subject: CARP (640M)
rows.operation_detail: Compared uncertainty for repeated protein units by unit length.
rows.value: The model exhibits uncertainty collapse for repeating units shorter than approximately 70 residues.
rows.note: The paper describes a length-dependent transition in this model.
rows.check: CARP is convolutional with no attention heads; cannot bear on a head-based version. Baseline is the 1x sequence, not 'not stated'.

source_check.correct: Baseline: the original 1x protein sequence; comparison: doubled sequences with repeating units shorter than approximately 70 residues.
source_check.problem: The experiment compares repeated sequences with their 1x originals; the baseline is not unstated.

rows.subject: CARP (640M)
rows.operation_detail: Compared uncertainty for repeated protein units by unit length.
rows.value: For larger repeating units, the model shows a progressive decline in uncertainty rather than collapse.
rows.note: The paper describes the approximate 70-residue threshold as an operational-memory limit.

rows.subject: CARP (640M)
rows.operation_detail: Compared uncertainty as multiplicity increased for random repeating units.
rows.value: A complete uncertainty collapse is reported for repeating units of size 20.
rows.note: The text does not give exact plotted values.

rows.subject: CARP (640M)
rows.operation_detail: Compared uncertainty as multiplicity increased for random repeating units.
rows.value: Repeating units of size 70 show heightened sensitivity to multiplicity.
rows.note: The paper characterizes this as the boundary between collapse and progressive decline.
rows.check: Convolutional model; text says 'heightened sensitivity to multiplicity', not a weaker effect.

rows.subject: CARP (640M)
rows.operation_detail: Compared uncertainty as multiplicity increased for random repeating units.
rows.value: Uncertainty declines progressively as multiplicity increases, without a complete collapse.
rows.note: The paper contrasts this with the collapse for 20-residue units.

rows.subject: LC-PLM (1.4B)
rows.operation_detail: Compared pseudo-perplexity as random repeating-unit multiplicity increased.
rows.value: No complete uncertainty collapse, even at 32x; pseudo-perplexity declines steadily, most for the shortest units.
rows.note: The decline weakens as repeating-unit size increases.
rows.check: BiMamba-S model with no attention heads.

rows.subject: ESM2 (650M)
rows.stage_stated: trained on the masked language modeling objective
rows.operation_detail: Masked a residue in one copy of a domain and compared predictions with a second copy present.

conditions.value: one position in the first copy; equivalent position in the second copy unmasked

rows.measure: Entropy of the masked-position probability vector
rows.value: The model's confidence increases when the equivalent position in the second copy is available; masking that equivalent position disrupts the confidence.
rows.note: The paper interprets this as retrieval of the corresponding residue from the other copy.
rows.check: Behavioural look-up evidence; no head or circuit is identified.

rows.subject: ESM2 (650M)
rows.stage_stated: trained on the masked language modeling objective
rows.operation_detail: Added a mask at a non-equivalent position in the second copy.

conditions.value: target position in first copy plus non-equivalent position in second copy

rows.measure: Confidence / entropy of the target-position prediction
rows.baseline: Target position masked with the second copy unmasked
rows.value: The model maintains its confidence when a non-equivalent position in the second copy is masked.
rows.note: This is the paper's control for the effect of adding an extra mask.

rows.subject: ESM2 (650M)
rows.stage_stated: trained on the masked language modeling objective
rows.operation_detail: Changed the residue at the equivalent position in the second copy and measured the target prediction.

conditions.value: several thousand protein domains and randomly generated sequences

rows.measure: Probability assigned to the substituted residue at the masked position
rows.value: Predictions skew toward the residue present at the equivalent position in the second copy; the probability profile is concentrated on diagonal entries for both domains and random sequences.
rows.note: For natural domains, the flipping response is weaker for W and C; this exception is not observed for random sequences.

rows.subject: ESM2 (650M)
rows.stage_stated: trained on the masked language modeling objective
rows.operation_detail: Presented two possible retrieval positions created by an insertion and compared preference by target position.
rows.measure: Preference between the two candidate retrieval residues
rows.value: At the left end, the model prefers the residue on the right.
rows.note: The paper says the contra-lateral preference manifests at extreme sequence ends.
rows.check: Retrieval-position quirk; not a version's measure.

rows.subject: ESM2 (650M)
rows.stage_stated: trained on the masked language modeling objective
rows.operation_detail: Scored a mutated copy of a protein domain with and without the natural copy as context.

conditions.value: natural protein domains with progressively divergent appended copies
substitutions, insertions and deletions; half the positions in the other copy can differ

rows.measure: Local OFS pseudo-perplexity of the mutated copy
rows.value: Local pseudo-perplexity is significantly lower when the mutated copy appears alongside the natural copy.
rows.note: The paper states that retrieval persists for imperfect repeats.

rows.subject: ESM2 (650M)
rows.stage_stated: trained on the masked language modeling objective
rows.operation_detail: Tested whether an identical random needle at the far end informs prediction for the first needle.

conditions.value: unrelated random sequence spanning hundreds of residues

rows.measure: Local pseudo-perplexity of the first needle
rows.value: The model reliably retrieves needles as small as 10 residues across haystacks spanning hundreds of residues.
rows.note: The paper reports an operational memory of approximately 1000 residues; it does not recognize larger repeats.

rows.subject: ESM2 (650M)
rows.stage_stated: trained on the masked language modeling objective
rows.operation_detail: Measured predictions on randomly generated one-skip sequence pairs with no perfectly matching chunks.

conditions.value: one-skip sequence pairs; matching residues in alternating positions
four contiguous masked positions and an average over thousands of one-at-a-time masked profiles

rows.measure: Probability mass assigned to the equivalent-position residue
rows.value: The model assigns high probability mass to equivalent-position residues throughout one-skip sequences, with correct-residue probabilities spiking according to the construction.
rows.note: The paper interprets this as retrieval that does not rely exclusively on contiguous matching segments.

rows.subject: ESM2 (650M) embeddings with MLP models
rows.operation_detail: Regressed one-at-a-time masked profiles from embeddings of repeated sequences and matched random-extension controls.

conditions.value: 5 runs with different training-validation splits; 80-20 split

rows.measure: MLP validation cross-entropy loss as a proxy for embedding information content
rows.baseline: Embeddings from matched control sequences with one natural protein copy followed by randomly generated sequence; 1x embeddings and one-hot vectors also used as baselines
rows.value: Higher-multiplicity embeddings have higher validation loss than their controls, and loss increases with multiplicity; the effect is stronger than appending random sequence.
rows.uncertainty: Curves averaged over 5 runs; no error bar or other uncertainty value stated.
rows.note: This is an embedding-quality result, not a measurement of head formation or of the claim's specified in-context-learning outcomes.

relation.reason: The authors compare retrieval behavior with induction heads while explicitly leaving the underlying bidirectional circuits unresolved.

tranche.reason: The study measures model-level biological-sequence retrieval and uncertainty, without identifying induction heads, testing their formation, or manipulating training conditions to test their emergence or persistence.

source_check.notes: No head-level mechanism is established. Figure 2 uses 1000 sampled protein domains shorter than 400 residues; Progen2-M uses perplexity rather than pseudo-perplexity.

statements.correction: ESM2 (8M, 650M): doubled sequences induce pseudo-perplexity collapse to approximately 1. Progen2-M: perplexity declines significantly, without complete collapse. RiNALMo (33.5M, 650M): direct repeats induce uncertainty collapse. ESM2 (650M): retrieved residues can override learned priors. CARP (640M): uncertainty collapse for repeating units shorter than approximately 70 residues.
statements.problem: The shared collapse-to-about-1 description incorrectly includes Progen2-M, whose perplexity declines without complete collapse. Overriding learned priors is directly tested in ESM2 (650M), not all listed models.
